title: Choose Zed or VS Code inside diffStory
summary: Start with the shared menu's load, save, and keyboard behavior, then follow it into the three product surfaces. Finish on the responsive geometry and focused contract tests; slow down on the unexercised network-failure state and the intentionally tighter mobile review chrome.

intent.goal: Let reviewers keep both Zed and VS Code available and choose their source-jump destination from a visible place inside diffStory.
intent.design: One shared radio menu reads and saves the machine-local editor preference, then appears beside the theme control on the picker, repository navigation, and review toolbar. Shared and review-specific CSS collapse the control without introducing horizontal overflow.
nonGoals: Deliberately does not change the existing Command- or Ctrl-click source-jump gesture; it only makes the destination selectable.

hotspots.reason: The success path was exercised in the browser and the failure copy is pinned statically, but I did not force a live network failure while the menu was open.
At 320px the editor control moves out of the review toolbar to protect the existing 44px actions; the choice remains available on Home, but that tradeoff merits a product glance.

storyScope.reviewerNote: Focused follow-up: the existing primary story covers the editor preference, source-jump bridge, and Zed extension. This story covers the newly visible chooser, its placement, responsive behavior, and direct tests.

steps.title: The shared menu begins from the persisted editor
steps.why: Start here: every surface mounts this component, which owns one editor vocabulary and loads the current machine preference before naming the trigger.

beats.text: The menu permits only Zed or VS Code, so the browser cannot invent a destination the server will reject.
One component owns preference, disclosure, progress, failure, and announcement state for every placement that follows.
The initial request resolves the saved choice while preserving an actionable error if settings are unavailable.

steps.title: Dismissal keeps focus behavior explicit
steps.why: Once the choice is loaded, the menu distinguishes dismissals that should restore trigger focus from pointer and Tab exits that should continue naturally.

beats.text: The close helper restores focus only when the interaction contract asks for it, preventing a Tab exit from snapping backward.
Opening focuses the checked item, so keyboard review starts from the editor that is actually active.
An outside pointer press closes without stealing the pointer's next destination, matching the Tab behavior reviewed later.

steps.title: Selection persists before the menu claims success
steps.why: The chooser does not optimistically rename itself. It waits for the settings endpoint, announces the saved label, and leaves a failed menu open for retry.

beats.text: Re-selecting the active editor closes immediately, while a real change enters one busy state and sends only the next editor value.
The resolved server label updates the trigger before success is announced; a rejected save instead preserves the menu and exposes retry copy.

steps.title: Keyboard exits and radio movement have separate jobs
steps.why: Tab closes and advances, Escape closes and restores focus, and directional keys stay inside the two-item radio menu without changing the preference prematurely.

beats.text: Tab deliberately keeps its browser default while Escape consumes the key and returns to the trigger, closing the reviewer's reported focus gap.
Arrow and boundary keys move focus through the available radios; only activation reaches the save path above.

steps.title: The visible control exposes one complete menu contract
steps.why: This markup ties the loaded label, menu disclosure, checked radio, retry action, and quiet live announcement into one reusable control before it is placed around the product.

beats.text: The trigger names the actual destination and publishes menu disclosure state even when its compact placement hides visible text.
The menu explains the source-jump gesture and exposes each destination as a checked radio rather than unrelated action buttons.
Failure remains retryable in place, while save progress and success use a dedicated polite status instead of announcing on every page load.

steps.title: Repository navigation keeps the choice beside theme
steps.why: Now that the menu contract is complete, the shared repository bar places it immediately before theme so history and change-selection pages inherit the choice automatically.

beats.text: Skim this shared placement: repository pages gain the same editor control without duplicating state or endpoint logic.

steps.title: The picker lets the menu escape its decorative masthead
steps.why: The Home surface is the fallback placement even on the narrowest review layout. Its masthead must allow the anchored menu to escape instead of clipping it at the section edge.

beats.text: The picker imports the shared control and releases the masthead overflow boundary, so the popover can extend beyond the decorative hero.

steps.title: Picker actions collapse before the brand overflows
steps.why: The selector and theme now share one right-side plate, while the nonessential tagline yields below 400px so both controls remain reachable without horizontal scrolling.

beats.text: The descriptive kicker yields first on very narrow screens, preserving the product name and interactive actions.
Editor and theme controls share one surfaced group, making the new preference discoverable without reading as a page-specific action.

steps.title: Review chrome reuses the compact selector
steps.why: The review surface uses the same stateful menu in compact form beside theme, keeping story navigation dominant while leaving source destination one click away.

beats.text: Skim this second shared placement: the review toolbar gets the same chooser with an icon-only trigger and no parallel preference state.

steps.title: The trigger and popover inherit product geometry
steps.why: Placement now hands off to presentation: the trigger uses existing pills and tokens, while the popover anchors above page content with a viewport-bounded width.

beats.text: The wrapper and trigger stay flex-stable, preventing the new action from squeezing breadcrumbs or review tabs unpredictably.
Expanded, compact, hover, and focus states reuse the product's semantic tokens, so the control reads like a sibling of theme rather than an embedded extension badge.
The menu anchors to the trigger but caps itself against the viewport, closing the original hero-clipping failure without creating a full-screen sheet on desktop.

steps.title: Radio rows keep copy, target, and checked state aligned
steps.why: Inside the popover, a three-column row reserves stable space for the editor mark, two-line explanation, and checked indicator without shrinking the hit target.

beats.text: The heading separates the menu's purpose from its choices, so the two editor names do not have to carry gesture instructions.
Each radio row keeps a 54px target and a fixed status column, preventing checked state or longer VS Code copy from shifting alignment.
The remaining styles preserve readable secondary copy and reveal exactly one semantic check without introducing another color language.

steps.title: Failure, motion, and narrow-screen states stay bounded
steps.why: The tail of the shared control keeps failure actionable, disables motion when requested, and turns the anchored menu into an inset fixed surface below 560px.

beats.text: Save and load failures remain a full-width retry target with semantic danger colors instead of disappearing into the trigger title.
The pop animation is opt-in to motion preference, while reduced-motion users keep the same states with no transition dependency.
Below 560px the label collapses and the menu becomes a twelve-pixel inset fixed surface, which is the containment rule verified at 320px.

steps.title: Review chrome preserves desktop and touch target sizes
steps.why: The compact trigger matches the existing 36px desktop theme control and rises to a 44px target at the review toolbar's mobile breakpoint.

beats.text: Skim this paired sizing rule: the editor control follows the review chrome's established desktop and touch target geometry instead of defining a third size.

steps.title: The narrowest review toolbar yields the editor control
steps.why: At 470px and below, review tabs and the theme action keep their existing 44px contracts; source-editor selection remains available from Home rather than forcing toolbar overflow.

beats.text: Pause on this tradeoff: the smallest review toolbar hides only the editor wrapper, preserving the established tabs and theme target with no horizontal scroll.

steps.title: The selector suite reads every ownership surface
steps.why: The focused suite reads the component, every placement, and both CSS owners directly, so a removed integration point cannot hide behind a passing component-only assertion.

beats.text: The fixture loads the menu, all three product placements, and their responsive styles before any contract assertion runs.

steps.title: Choice tests pin persistence and radio semantics
steps.why: These assertions fail if either destination, the PUT request, checked-radio contract, accessible label, or successful save announcement disappears.

beats.text: The first test pins both editor values, the persistence call, radio selection semantics, and the label announced after a confirmed save.

steps.title: Boundary tests keep keyboard, retry, and reachability intact
steps.why: Final proof: the suite names every supported key, the reviewer's Tab fix, retry and live-region behavior, reduced motion, all placements, and the smallest review breakpoint.

beats.text: The keyboard test now fails if Tab stops closing without focus restoration, while the remaining assertions retain directional movement, retry, live status, focus styling, and reduced motion.
The reachability test closes the path by requiring picker, shared navigation, review placement, and the narrow-toolbar containment rule together.
